We wish to know," they asked, and the Blessed One said: "Monks, ninety-one eons ago in the past, the perfectly complete Buddha named Vipaśyin, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, charioteer who tames persons, unsurpassed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One, arose in the world and was dwelling in the royal city of Bandhumat. At that time one of the plasterer caste, called [unclear] Gagemo, built a monastery for Vipaśyin, planted flowering and fruit trees well, and it came to be filled all around with sweet fragrance; having offered it, he also went forth in the teaching of that very Teacher. After the perfectly complete Buddha Vipaśyin had passed into nirvāṇa, he raised a jewel pillar beneath the foundation of the stūpa of his relics. The large following of that one who had gone forth from the plasterer caste also rejoiced and became devoted: "Just as you became devoted to the Teacher, so I too have faith and devotion; I act according to the Teacher's command and do what pleases, and what does not please
